sections.heading: Profile
sections.text: Embedded systems engineer with six years of firmware and board bring-up for battery-powered sensor products, from first prototype to certified volume production. Comfortable owning a product's electronics end to end and working across mechanical, software and test teams.

groups.label: Firmware
groups.text: C, C++17, FreeRTOS, Zephyr; STM32, nRF52, ESP32; bootloaders, OTA updates; SPI, I²C, UART, BLE, LoRaWAN.

groups.label: Hardware
groups.text: Schematic capture and PCB layout in KiCad and Altium Designer; power budgets, battery management, EMC pre-compliance.

groups.label: Test & automation
groups.text: Python test fixtures, pytest, hardware-in-the-loop rigs; oscilloscope, logic analyser, power profiler; CI with GitHub Actions.

groups.label: Process
groups.text: Design reviews, DFM with contract manufacturers, CE/RED certification support, Git, Jira.

bullets: Owned firmware and electronics for a LoRaWAN soil-moisture sensor shipped to 40,000 sites.
Cut average current draw from 48 µA to 11 µA, extending battery life from 2 to 7 years.
Built a Python hardware-in-the-loop rig running 300 regression tests on every merge.
Developed BLE firmware for a wearable heart-rate monitor through CE certification.
Wrote PLC and HMI logic for packaging lines; commissioned three lines on site.

letter.subject: Application: Embedded Systems Engineer
paragraphs: Open with why this company and this role, using specifics from the posting itself rather than generic praise. Name the product, the team, or the problem the advertisement actually describes, and say what draws you to it. Two or three sentences is enough: the reader is deciding whether to keep reading, not grading your enthusiasm.

Match your experience against the tasks the posting actually lists, in the posting's own vocabulary, and ground every claim in something real: a system you built, a number you measured, a method you ran. Lead with the closest match rather than the most impressive one. Then close this paragraph by naming the one requirement you do not yet meet, plainly and without apology, for example: "I have not worked with X before, but I have moved into unfamiliar technical domains several times and I get productive quickly." Naming the gap yourself is more convincing than hoping it goes unnoticed.

Finish with what you are like to work with, using facts rather than adjectives: teams led, people mentored, cross-functional collaborations. If you have a portfolio page, link it once here, tied to something you already argued; for example, the sensor platform is documented at [alexsample.example/projects](https://alexsample.example/projects). Close by inviting the conversation.
